Guidance & outlook: With a population of more than 1.4 billion, a predominantly young consumer base, rising disposable incomes, rapid urbanization and increasing exposure to global fashion trends, the demand for footwear is expected to continue expanding.

Terms and conditions of appointment/re- appointment Proposed appointment as Executive Director, liable to retire by rotation Details of remuneration to be sought/ remuneration last drawn (2025-26) He has drawn remuneration of `30 Lakh P .A. during the FY 2025-26.

Outlook Your Directors believe that the domestic footwear industry remains well positioned for long-term growth, supported by rising formalization, evolving consumer preferences, increasing demand for branded and value- for-money products, and the recent GST rationalization on footwear up to ₹2,500 per pair.
Growth & demand: During the Financial Year 2025-26, the Company achieved a turnover of ₹73,999.11 Lakhs, registering a growth of 9.55% over ₹67 ,548.06 Lakhs in the previous year.

The GST rationalization on footwear priced up to ₹2,500 per pair, from 12% to 5% with effect from September 22, 2025, was a positive development for the industry and supported affordability and consumer demand.

Notwithstanding the moderation in profitability, the Company maintained growth in revenue of 9.55%, reflecting the resilience of its diversified business model and continued traction across key business segments.
Margins & costs: Anupam Bansal, Executive Director of the Company. costs, increase in minimum wages and the consequent increase in employee benefit costs, along with other operating costs pressures.

The moderation in profitability, despite revenue growth, was primarily attributable to continued pressure on input and raw material costs, regular increases in minimum wages and the consequent increase in employee benefit costs, along with other operating cost pressures during the year.

While near-term challenges may persist from input cost pressures, wage and employee benefit costs and fluctuations in consumer demand, the Company remains committed to improving productivity, optimizing its cost structure and strengthening margins while delivering quality products, enhanced customer experience and value for money to its consumers.

Retail Expansion and Store Modernization The Company continued its retail expansion during the year, with a focused approach towards tier-II and tier-III cities through a combination of Company-owned, franchised and distribution-led formats, taking its network of exclusive retail outlets beyond 475-plus stores.

Further to note that if the aforesaid details are not received and the dividend remains unpaid/unclaimed upto 7 years, dividend will be transferred to IEPF after 7 years as per the applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013.

Risk Management Policy & Risk Management The Management of the Company has always been consciously reviewing its business operations in accordance with set rules and procedure and if any deviation or risk is found, remedial and corrective steps are taken to minimize such deviation and risk.
The Board of Directors of the Company assesses several types of risks which include Business Environment Risks, Strategic Business Risks, Market Risk and Operational Risks etc.
